newsitem.title: USA: Mass. House committee approves $685 mln court bond.
newsitem.headline: Mass. House committee approves $685 mln court bond.

text.p: The Massachusetts House of Representatives is expected to take up debate Wednesday on a $685 million bond issue to rebuild the Commonwealth's aging network of courthouses.
The House Ways and Means Committee approved the measure on Tuesday, State House News Service reported.

The bill, appoved late on Tuesday, mirrors one that cleared the House last June, according to Ways and Means Chairman Paul Haley, D-Weymouth, and died at the end of the session when the House and Senate could not agree on its terms.
It is based on a $583 million bond authorization bill that Gov. William Weld filed last week.
"My understanding is that the Senate is interested in moving very quickly on this too," Haley told reporters following the committee's action.

The new measure authorizes the state to borrow $270 million for design work on a new facility for the Plymouth Trial Court, a court complex for downtown Worcester, and for renovations to the Suffolk County courthouse.

Another $225 million is for the renovation or replacement of existing facilities in Salem, Norfolk, Lowell, Lynn, Newton, Plymouth and South Boston as well as construction of new courthouses in Berkshire County, Falmouth, Belchertown, Franklin County, Middlesex County and Westfield.
There is another $143 million for county courthouses and $47.3 million for what the committee calls life safety repairs.
